items.title: Launch timing:
items.summary: Pre-launch chatter came first. @kimmonismus reported it already routing to his account, and @scaling01 spotted it in the Anthropic API before the official post.

items.title: Official announcement:
items.summary: @claudeai (53K engagement) and @AnthropicAI called it “a clear upgrade over Sonnet 5.” They claim it runs more than 30% faster and costs up to 30% less for most work.

items.title: Positioning:
items.summary: @ClaudeDevs positions it for “well-scoped everyday tasks like fixing bugs and quickly iterating on features.” Anthropic also published a build guide covering when to pick Sonnet vs. Opus 5.5, migrating from Sonnet 5, and tuning effort.

items.title: Anti-distillation change:
items.summary: @ClaudeDevs extended “preserved thinking” to counter distillation via account-switching. Reasoning traces stay in the org that generated them. If a session moves to another account, Claude rereads it and regenerates thinking.

items.title: Availability:
items.summary: It shipped day-one on the Claude Platform and Claude Code, along with a usage reset valid until Oct 22 ( @ClaudeDevs ). Third-party availability: GitHub Copilot in VS Code ( @code )

items.title: Anthropic releases Claude Sonnet 5.5:
items.summary: Their new and improved Claude Sonnet 5.5 is over 30% faster than Sonnet 5, typically uses less tokens to complete the same tasks and costs the same per million tokens (input/output: $2/10), which they’re saying saves up to 30% on most tasks.

items.title: A bit of bad news for OpenAI:
items.summary: They’ve pulled their new model, GPT-6.1 Astra prior to releasing it. Not because it’s too powerful, but because:

items.title: Manus is back with 2.0, plus something called Cue:
items.summary: Manus 2.0 is basically a rebuild of the whole thing. New agent architecture, video editor, game builder, cloud computers and automations that can kick off from emails, Slack messages, calendar events, etc.
